account-wide-agent-grant-01.graded_text: The design gives the agent connection a scope covering every workspace the person belongs to now or later plus documents shared with them individually, and does not make the person pick one organization per connection.

votes.e: C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:11 "**One agent connection covers all of a person's workspaces.** An MCP grant acts as the person, not as one of their workspaces." Line 78: "Join a new client workspace and the agent can use it on its next call." Line 19: the agent principal reaches the "Same as the person", which line 18 defines as "Their workspace memberships and their document shares".

account-wide-agent-grant-02.graded_text: Every tool call resolves the target workspace or document and checks live membership, role, and individual share on the server at call time. A single organization claim in a token is not treated as proof of access to any other workspace.

votes.e: C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:45 "The role or share allows the capability on the target resource. The target's workspace comes from the stored document, never from the caller." Line 77: "The gate never reads a workspace from the token, so it does not matter whether the provider puts an active organization in it." Line 78: "Each call is checked against the person's role **at call time**."

account-wide-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The create tool takes an explicit destination workspace ID, and the server verifies the caller may create in that workspace before creating. The design does not say a client-supplied workspace ID must never be used.

votes.e: C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:128 "`workspace` is **required**: a workspace ID from `list_workspaces`. There is no default workspace..." Line 131: "Requires `document.create` in that workspace". The closest line to forbidding a client-supplied ID is line 45, "The target's workspace comes from the stored document, never from the caller", but that concerns document targets. Line 10 says explicitly that when creating, "they have to name it".

account-wide-agent-grant-04.graded_text: Removing a membership or an individual share takes effect for an already connected agent without reconnecting.

votes.e: C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:78 "Get removed and the agent loses it the moment the membership webhook arrives. Nothing is copied into the grant, so nothing goes stale." Shares live in the database (line 24, "The database owns shares"), and the gate checks "The role or share allows the capability" on every request (lines 42-45). Removing a share therefore takes effect on the agent's next call with no reconnect.

account-wide-agent-grant-05.graded_text: An individually shared document gives access to that document only, never to its workspace's other documents or member list, through the UI and the agent alike.

votes.e: C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:24 "A share never gives access to anything else in the workspace: no listing, no other documents, no member list." Line 103: "For shared documents, `workspace` is `null` so that a share reveals nothing about the workspace it came from". Line 162: share recipients use the top-level `/documents/<id>` route, "without passing through a workspace they cannot see".

account-wide-agent-grant-06.graded_text: The library shows documents from every workspace the person belongs to by default, with workspace and shared filters held in URL query state, filters only narrow what is shown, and no active-workspace session state is introduced as an authority for browsing or for the agent connection.

votes.e: C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:12 "`/documents` shows documents from all your workspaces plus documents shared with you ... You narrow it with filters in the URL. There is no switcher in the header." Line 166: "Each is a link that filters the library. None of them changes any session state." Line 168: URL state `q`, `workspace=<id>`, `shared=true`. Line 180: "Nothing outside those pages reads the provider's active organization."

account-wide-agent-grant-07.graded_text: The design introduces no per-seat price and no paid seat gate, and leaves the member cap of 25 as the brief states it. A design that does not discuss billing or the cap passes.

votes.e: Searched C/project/docs/workspace-access.md and C/answer.txt for 'seat': no hits. The closest line is C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:182 "**Member cap 25**: a fixed constant in code, the same on every plan", which leaves the cap as the brief states it. Line 49: "Plan billing stays out of this gate."

account-wide-agent-grant-08.graded_text: The design says the consent screen states the connection's scope, including workspaces joined later.

votes.e: The only consent-screen line in C/project/docs/workspace-access.md that describes this design is line 66, "The consent screen asks for both by default", and it concerns the read/write scopes. Line 74 mentions a consent screen only for the competitor's pattern ("consent screen selects one organization"). Nothing says the consent screen tells the person that the connection reaches every workspace, including ones joined later.

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] The consent screen never discloses the account-wide reach. C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:80 admits "Accepted cost: a leaked token reaches every workspace the person belongs to", yet the consent screen is specified only as "asks for both [scopes] by default" (line 66). A person approving the connection is never told it covers all current and future client workspaces.

[opus-for-opus2] Agent writes can silently overwrite a person's concurrent edits, and the fix is deferred instead of chosen. C/project/docs/workspace-access.md:120 "Replaces the content." Line 205 leaves this open: "an agent can overwrite a person who is editing at the same moment. A base-version check would refuse a stale write. Decide before agents are widely used." As written, a cross-workspace agent ships with last-writer-wins full replacement.
